workoutList.description: A strength-training routine you can do anywhere. Complete as many rounds as possible in 10 minutes.

Learn to move one segment at a time.Articulation of the spine-moving one vertebra at a time-is a foundational movement in Pilates. It wakes up the core and develops awareness to the connection between the abdominals and the spine.
Strengthen your abs and work your arms and legs with this five-minute core burner. This no-equipment plank workout is quick and effective.
Slow 5k
Warm up, run and walk with strong effort, cool down.

workoutList.description:
Today is tough! We're going to establish your baseline fitness so that we can help you set your training zones and be able to track your progress.
-
Warm up for at least 15 minutes with some medium intensity surges. Then do a 20-minute race-like effort on a course with light traffic, few intersections and no stoplights. It should be mostly flat or slightly uphill (2-3% grade).
-
Maintain the highest speed/effort possible for the entire 20 minutes. Finish with a short cool down spin at an easy pace.
-
Make sure you record your average heart rate and average power (AP) for the 20-minute effort.
-
After the workout, multiply your 20-min AP (and average HR) by 0.95 to determine your Functional Threshold Power (FTP) Functional Threshold Heart Rate (FTHR). Zones may be set up for the bike (heart rate and/or power) by using these final numbers. For a more detailed explanation of how to set zones go to: http://www.trainingbible.com/joesblog/2009/11/quick-guide-to-setting-zones.html.

Warm up, building from zone 1 to zone 2; keep cadence over 85 rpm
-
You're likely feeling yesterday's effort, and that's ok because today shouldn't be too hard. You'll ride steady (zone 2/RPE 5) for 45 min but if that's feeling like a bit too much, feel free to cut this ride short or lower the intensity. Use the entire zone - don't just ride the top of it; keep cadence 85-95 throughout.
Head out for an easy ride at a moderate pace. The effort should feel like a 4/10 - in other words, you should be able to breathe through your nose and hold a conversation.

Warm up, building from Zone 1 to Zone 2; keep cadence over 85 rpm.
-
Steady Zone 2 for ~120min depending on time allowed. Use the entire zone - don't just ride the top of it; keep cadence 85-95 throughout.
-
Cool down.
